🈁️**Resolved as of Nov 17–18, 2026.**[]
(<https://t.co/RLGCUF9zYO>)

JPMorgan Chase’s Nov 16 outage (software bug in its on-premise hardware systems) is fixed. The bank confirmed transactions were processing normally by Monday evening (~6:30–7 p.m. ET). By Tuesday morning, services were back to normal (“business as usual”), with Downdetector reports returning to baseline and no widespread issues reported as of Nov 18.[]
(<https://t.co/Wx0yc7ygmg>)

### Key facts from official statements and coverage
- **Cause**: Temporary software bug in Chase’s own on-premise hardware (not cloud, not cyber-related, not a systemic banking crisis). Other banks (Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank, etc.) saw secondary delays mainly on transactions involving Chase accounts, including some Zelle activity. Zelle’s network itself was operational.[]
(<https://t.co/5w1PPjq5ik>)
- **Impact**: Slowed online/app logins, balance views, and some transactions for hours. Isolated branch and ATM reports of systems being down (tellers unable to process deposits/withdrawals temporarily). Peak Downdetector reports ~4,600–5,000 for Chase around 2 p.m. ET.
- **Funds and cash**: Chase repeatedly stated customers retained access to their accounts and funds throughout. There is no verified evidence of a physical cash shortage or branches “out of money”—those claims stem from anecdotal customer reports on DownDetector/social media about temporary system outages preventing normal teller transactions, not a liquidity problem.[]
(<https://t.co/7ALe8ym3VZ>)
- **Resolution timeline**: Chase aimed to fix it by end of Monday; confirmed normal processing that evening. Outlets (USA Today, NBC, Bloomberg, CNN, etc.) reported the issue cleared by late Nov 16 / early Nov 17.

No ongoing multi-bank outage or cash crisis is indicated in current reporting. If you’re still seeing local issues, try the app/website, an ATM, or contact Chase support—individual delays can lag after the main fix.🈁️

Should You Buy $NBIS at $107.36 after the Sell-off?

The latest earnings revisions on Wall Street reveal an interesting paradox.

Over the past few days, all 7 analysts covering Nebius have lowered their price targets:

• Northland Securities: $410 → $380
• Truist Financial: $355 → $245
• Robert W. Baird: $340 → $200
• Bank of America Securities: $310 → $265
• Citi: $265 → $215
• D.A. Davidson: $250 → $125 (Hold)
• Piper Sandler: $185 → $148 (Hold)

Despite this, the consensus rating remains “Buy,” and the average price target is $225.43.

Since the stock has fallen significantly more than analysts have revised their models, the potential upside from the $107.36 level reaches +110%.

Even the most conservative target from D.A. Davidson at $125 (Hold) still implies a +16.4% increase from current levels.

Key takeaway: Investment banks are adjusting their short-term expectations but are not abandoning their thesis on Neocloud.

The market is currently pricing in significant downside risks, while Wall Street continues to project a more than twofold recovery in the stock price.

🚨🇺🇸 Citibank prévient ses clients que si un agent d'IA tiers se fait pirater, ils paieront eux-mêmes les dégâts sur leur compte.

La banque a modifié ses conditions d'utilisation cette semaine. Les agents d'IA peuvent recevoir les identifiants d'un compte pour analyser des dépenses, conseiller sur des placements ou payer des factures. Citi estime désormais que le client est responsable de tout ce que fait l'agent, et de ce que font des pirates si l'outil fuite ses identifiants.

Citi n'est pas seule. JPMorgan et Bank of America, les deux plus grandes banques du pays, ont annoncé des règles similaires le mois dernier. PNC a modifié les siennes aujourd'hui, et Citizens a prévenu ses clients par e-mail, d'après TechCrunch.

L'outil de finances personnelles lancé par Anthropic ce mois-ci est présenté comme en « lecture seule » : il ne peut ni déplacer, ni gérer, ni investir l'argent.
